slice: The shark encounter, part 1: legacy's roll timer, spawn, pass and contact roll in the core on the dive's seeded random state, its game-over text in English and German, save v16, and the recorded legacy dive with scripted rolls it is replayed against. The sprite and the client's wiring are part 2.

results.distCheck: pass: 17 files scanned, no source maps, 4 diagnostic markers absent.
results.unit: 487 passed (470 on main, +12 in tests/unit/shark-encounter.test.ts, +5 in tests/unit/save-game.test.ts)
results.parity: 266 passed (241 on main, +4 in tests/parity/shark-encounter.test.ts, +7 each in dive-grade, dive-planner and post-dive, which run one test per recorded checkpoint and pick up the seven new ones)
results.e2e: 146 passed in 5.5 min (145 on main, +1 in tests/game-over.spec.js: the shark screen)

portedFromTheOracle.timer: src/game-loop.js TASK-043: sharkTimer counts down in dive seconds and, at or below zero, is set to 60 (src/state.js's initial and resetDive() value), dropping what the tick overran, and rolls.
portedFromTheOracle.spawn: `!shark && Math.random() < 0.005 && !noShark`: the roll is drawn only while no shark swims, before the site's noShark is read; then the heading (`< 0.5` right) and the depth, depth + (r * 20 - 10) clamped to 0..MAX_DEPTH (300). It starts (cssWidth * DIVER_SCREEN_X_FRACTION + 100) * 0.05 m behind its heading: half the view plus 5 m, DIVER_SCREEN_X_FRACTION being 0.5.
portedFromTheOracle.swim: x moves by direction * speed * dtReal, real seconds, 7.5 m/s (2.5 * 0.05 * 60); the depth moves toward the diver's by 0.3 m per dive second when more than 0.1 m off, then stays FAUNA_AVOID_MARGIN (0.5 m) above floorAt(x).
portedFromTheOracle.contact: `!passed && |x - diverX| < 2 && |depth - diverDepth| < 3`: passed is set, one roll, under 0.33 the dive ends with SHARK ATTACK and nothing else of the tick runs; otherwise the speed becomes 12 m/s (4 * 0.05 * 60). The shark is removed beyond half the view plus 7.5 m (150 px) in its heading.
portedFromTheOracle.order: The shark runs after the frame's other updates and before updateDiving()'s game-over checks, so it comes before out of gas; the rebreather checks return before it.
portedFromTheOracle.text: STRINGS.{en,de}.gameOverReasons and gameOverInfo['SHARK ATTACK'], taken verbatim from src/constants.js and checked by evaluating it in a Node vm, the label in the catalogue's sentence case, as gameOver.reason.sharkAttack and gameOver.info.sharkAttack.*; anchored under SHARK-001 and GAMEOVER-001 for both locales.

decisions: The rolls come from the dive's seeded randomState (src/core/rng.ts), drawn in legacy's order, so a replay is deterministic. Legacy draws from Math.random, so parity covers the deterministic parts and the outcome of a given roll: advanceShark() takes the draws as a function, and the parity test passes legacy's scripted rolls.

The model holds no horizontal position, so the shark is held relative to the diver: offsetM is legacy's shark.x - diverX. DiveEnvironment.shark brings what the shark needs from the world, as rates: the time multiplier (the shark swims in real time), the diver's horizontal velocity per dive second, half the view's width in metres, the floor under the shark, and the site's noShark. Without it no shark is simulated and nothing is drawn. The route position (#222) need not be saved for it.
The client does not pass DiveEnvironment.shark yet: a shark that can end a dive arrives with its sprite, in part 2.

Save v16: older saves resume as a new dive does (60 s to the first roll, no shark) and one claiming a shark attack is refused; legacy saves keep a positive finite sharkTimer and resume with no shark, as legacy, which does not save the shark. Validation requires a positive finite timer and, when one swims, a finite offset, a non-negative depth, a heading of 1 or -1, a positive speed and a boolean passed.
A shark attack is valid with the DCS timer at its limit, as out of gas and oxygen toxicity are: legacy checks it first.
parity: shark-encounter-5m scripts legacy's rolls through the baseline's Math.random stub, one value for every draw of a tick, at 5 m on air with the view pinned 1000 px wide: three rolls at 0.5, a spawn at 0.004 (heading right, 9.92 m up, clamped to the surface), contact survived at 0.5, the shark gone past the view, a second spawn, and an attack at 0.2. advanceShark() replays it tick by tick with the same rolls at the depth legacy read back: the timer, offset, depth, heading, speed and passed match at every checkpoint, and the attack lands on legacy's last tick and on no earlier one. In the full model the timer reaches legacy's 39 s through three rolls with exactly three draws from the random state, and the recorded game over restores as a shark attack that goes no further. Not comparable: legacy's random stream itself.

counterChecks.method: Each revert was applied to the working copy, tests/unit/shark-encounter.test.ts, tests/parity/shark-encounter.test.ts and tests/unit/save-game.test.ts were run, and the file was restored; the tree was clean afterwards. The first set let two reverts pass (a roll on every step inside the window, and the exit at 5 m); 4c216a3 adds the tests that catch them, and the results below are from the run after it.

deferred: Part 2 of #219: the shark sprite in the Pixi scene and the client passing DiveEnvironment.shark. Open owner question: the client seeds every wreck dive with the constant 0x57524543, whose first spawn roll is the 193rd, so no shark would appear in a real dive without a per-dive seed.
